purpose:

received in respect of the advertised proposals for waiting
restrictions on Stanley Park Close and to determine whether the
proposed restrictions should be implemented as originally
advertised.
content:

received in respect of the advertised proposals for waiting
restrictions on Stanley Park Close and to determine whether the
proposed restrictions should be implemented as originally
advertised.

The Cabinet Member agreed the
recommendations as outlined above namely:

received in respect of the proposed waiting restrictions on Stanley
Park Close.

restrictions on Stanley Park Close as originally advertised, having
given due consideration to the representations received and the
highway conditions at the location.

authorise the Head of Legal Services to seal the Order
incorporating the necessary amendment to omit the Stanley Park

received, will proceed as originally advertised.

purpose:
To seek
approval for the advertisement and implementation of a
Permanent
Traffic
Regulation Order:
 
THE BOROUGH OF BLACKPOOL (VARIOUS ROADS) (CONSOLIDATION OF
WAITING RESTRICTIONS, ON STREET PARKING PLACES, RESIDENTS’
PARKING PLACES AND TAXI STANDS) (AMENDMENT No 12) ORDER

Order”).
content:
To seek
approval for the advertisement and implementation of a
Permanent
Traffic
Regulation Order:
 
THE BOROUGH OF BLACKPOOL (VARIOUS ROADS) (CONSOLIDATION OF
WAITING RESTRICTIONS, ON STREET PARKING PLACES, RESIDENTS’
PARKING PLACES AND TAXI STANDS) (AMENDMENT No 12) ORDER
2026 (“the Amendment No 12
Order”).
 

To
authorise the statutory consultation and advertisement of the
Council’s
intention
to make a Traffic Regulation Order under the Road Traffic
Regulation
Act 1984,
the effect of which will be to introduce or amend parking
restrictions
on various
roads throughout Blackpool, as detailed within the
background
information and appendices and summarised below:

·      
No Waiting at Any Time restrictions on various
roads;

·      
Disabled parking places, Monday to Saturday, 8.00am
to 6.00pm, on Central Drive;

·      
Limited Waiting parking place, Monday to Saturday,
8.00am to 6.00pm, on Central Drive; and

·      
Limited Waiting parking place, 9.00am to 11.00pm, on
Rutherford Place, with a maximum stay of 1 hour and no return
within 2 hours.
 
If no objections are received,
or if objections received are subsequently withdrawn, to authorise
the Head of Legal Services to make the Traffic Regulation
Order.

The Executive agreed the
recommendations as outlined above namely:
 
1.      
To note the report.  
 

2.     
To require the respective directors and Chief
Executive to continue to closely monitor and manage service
financial and operational performances of Council services and the
wholly-owned companies.
 

3.     
To note the Scrutiny Leadership Board will continue
to independently review the financial and operational performances
of Council services.
 

4.     
To continue to lobby central government
(Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Department
for Health and Social Care and Department for Education in
particular) along with local authority peers and networks and the
Local Government Association for the funding necessary to cope with
the burdens and demands presenting as a result of inflationary
pressures and demographic demands upon statutory services.
 
5.     
To continue to work towards target working balances
of £7.8m by 1 April 2027.

purpose:
To inform the Cabinet Member of
the findings from the updated Sheltered Review and make
recommendations for future changes.
content:
To inform the Cabinet Member of
the findings from the updated Sheltered Review and make
recommendations for future changes.
 

That the two schemes identified in section 6
of the report namely Tarnside and Washington Avenue be
de-commissioned and turned into general needs stock, and that this
should be done in a phased way.
 
That officers continue to review the
eligibility and support needs of working age tenants living in
sheltered housing, to ensure that allocations remain appropriate
and that residents’ needs are being met through the correct
housing and support arrangements.
 
That the Council and Blackpool Coastal Housing
review and right-size service charges for support, so that charges
are more reflective of the level of support provided to residents
who need it, with the outcome of this review feeding into the
Council’s budget-setting process in February next year.
 
That the Council and Blackpool Coastal Housing
continue to explore opportunities for new and replacement schemes,
such as those at Harvest Court and on Whitegate Drive, ensuring

content:
The Shareholder Committee
considered a report on the proposed Companies Group Policy
Framework for the Council’s wholly owned
companies.
 
Ms Annette Kerr, Head of Company Governance (Company
Secretary), presented the report to the Committee. Ms Kerr
explained that the policy framework formed a key part of the
overall governance framework of the Council’s Wholly-Owned
Companies but highlighted that the policy framework would be a
living document hence the recommendation at 2.4 of the report to
delegate the approval of future minor amendments. Ms Kerr concluded
her presentation by re-emphasising the purpose of the policy
framework namely to support good governance and effective
oversight, to promote consistency of approach where appropriate
across the group of wholly owned companies, to clarify expectations
regarding policy ownership, review and approval; and to support
companies in maintaining governance arrangements proportionate to
their operational activities and risks.
 
 
The Committee agreed that the
framework would ensure a consistent governance approach but would
also allow each company to tailor the arrangements to be
appropriate to their size and activities. In light of this
situation, while the Committee accepted that given the nature of
the company the policy framework might be of limited relevance to
Blackpool Airport Properties Limited but that the framework should
also be referred to that company’s board for
consideration. 
 
Resolved:
 

1.  To endorse the Companies Group
Policy Framework attached at Appendix 2a.
 

2.  To note that the Framework
establishes a consistent and proportionate governance approach
across the Council’s wholly owned companies whilst enabling
each company to adopt arrangements appropriate to its size,
activities and regulatory environment.
 

3.  To note that each company will
be responsible for adopting and maintaining its own policy
framework, for approval by its Board of Directors, having regard to
the principles contained within the Companies Group Policy
Framework.
 

4.  To delegate authority to the
Assistant Chief Executive (Governance) / Monitoring Officer, after
consultation with the Chair of the Shareholder Committee, to
approve future non-material amendments to the Framework. Any
material amendments shall be brought back to the Committee for
approval.
 
Reason for
Decision:
 
The Council’s wholly
owned companies play an important role in delivering the
Shareholder’s strategic priorities. It is therefore
appropriate for the Shareholder Committee to endorse a consistent
governance framework which promotes good governance,
accountability, transparency and effective oversight across the
group whilst recognising the differing operational requirements of
individual companies.
 
Alternative Options
Rejected:
 
The Committee noted that an alternative option would be to not adopt a
Group Policy Framework and instead allow each company to continue
developing policy arrangements independently, but agreed that this
option was not supportable as would reduce consistency across the
Group, increase the risk of duplication and governance gaps, and
make it more difficult for the Shareholder to obtain assurance
regarding governance standards across the wholly owned
companies.
 
Date of Decision:
 
28 July
2026
topline: The Shareholder Committee has decided to endorse a Companies Group Policy Framework to establish consistent governance across the Council's wholly owned companies.

content:
The report is provided in
response to the Executive Paper (EX39/2025 10th November
2025) and the decision to note the draft list of potential Pride in
Place Impact Fund schemes outlined in the report, and for the
approval of the final allocation of funding to be delegated to the
Director of Place, in consultation with the Leader of the
Council”. This is the first of what will be several Officer
Non-Key Decisions relating to projects to be included in the Pride
in Place Impact Fund programme, which will be brought forward for
approval as soon as they are ready to be implemented.
 
This report seeks formal
approval for £415,000 capital grant funding to be used to
fund various projects that will support businesses located in South
Shore.
 

That the sum of £415,000
from the Pride and Place Impact Fund is allocated to the following
projects:
 

a)     
South Shore
Commercial Improvement Fund – (Indicative allocation
£150k)

·      
Redlined District Area
of Waterloo Road and Lytham Road (See Appendix 1 – Map
Boundary)

·      
Qualifying retailers
to receive grants of up to £10k for improvements to
shopfronts.  The grants would normally
be 90% of the total value (unless there are exceptional
circumstances). Examples could include new windows, doors, painting
and security improvements (See Appendix 2 -  Application Form
Appendix 3 - 
Fund Guidance )

·      
Other buildings to
consider would be prominently placed empty units (privately owned)
where some aesthetic improvements could attract tenants to
otherwise empty units.  At least one
prominent building has been identified

 

b)    
Urban Greening
Scheme – ‘Grey to Green’
(Indicative
allocation £30k)

·      
A green scheme aimed
at turning grey areas into vibrant green spaces

·      
Using existing
structures e.g. lampposts, bus stops, telephone boxes and bins to
provide innovative ways of providing planting and making them more
visually appealing

·      
South Shore to be put
‘on the map’ for combining public realm with vibrant
and alternative planting and growing options

·      
The outcome would be
the creation of a South Shore In Bloom
group and a distinct brand for the area

 

c)     
Vibrant Streets
Lighting Scheme (Indicative allocation £55k)

·      
Lighting
infrastructure improvements to increase lighting options

·      
Increase level of
security and confidence for traders

·      
Provide an extension
to the illuminations/attract visitors and increase
footfall

·      
Additional lighting on
existing lampposts

·      
Option for new
lighting structures ‘Welcome to Waterloo’ / ‘Shopping This Way’
etc
 

d)    
Pathways to
Place (Indicative allocation £45k)

·      
Clearer and innovative
wayfinding from gateways towards the High Street.  Examples
include from South Shore train station,
both ends of Waterloo Road including the promenade

·      
Wayfinding to local
attractions and green / open spaces such as George Bancroft Park
and the beach / promenade

 

e)    
Walks and Walls
– Colours in Motion
(Indicative
allocation £35k)
•     Gable end / wall murals in and
around the high street
•     Pavement art / opportunity to
link to the wayfinding
•     Create wellbeing walks / trails
alongside innovative art and street canvases/    distinct pathways
 

f)      
Charity Shop
Improvement Scheme(indicative allocation £100k)
·      
Enables charity shops
to revamp exterior and interior space
·      
Improvements could
include new merchandising, new display cabinets, new décor
and better layout of products
·      
Local artists and
community creative groups could be involved in decorating and
designing spaces
·      
Creation of a Charity
Shop Trail to attract footfall to the area
topline: The Director of Place has decided to allocate £415,000 from the Pride in Place Impact Fund to support various projects aimed at enhancing businesses in South Shore.

Blackpool Catering
Service (BCS). It provides an overview of how the service has
evolved from its origins as a fully Local Authority supported
provision to its current position operating within an increasingly
competitive and uncertain market shaped by widespread school
academisation. The report also details the impact of academisation
on service sustainability, changing procurement behaviours within
academy trusts, and the resulting pressures on Blackpool Catering
Service’s ability to remain financially viable. It highlights
the significant reduction in schools served over time, recent
fluctuations linked to market forces, and the anticipated risks
associated with upcoming tender processes that may further affect
the long-term viability of the service.
content:
To outline the
operational history, current position, and future challenges
facing
Blackpool Catering
Service (BCS). It provides an overview of how the service has
evolved from its origins as a fully Local Authority supported
provision to its current position operating within an increasingly
competitive and uncertain market shaped by widespread school
academisation. The report also details the impact of academisation
on service sustainability, changing procurement behaviours within
academy trusts, and the resulting pressures on Blackpool Catering
Service’s ability to remain financially viable. It highlights
the significant reduction in schools served over time, recent
fluctuations linked to market forces, and the anticipated risks
associated with upcoming tender processes that may further affect
the long-term viability of the service.
 

The Cabinet Member
agreed the recommendations as outlined above namely:
 
           
That the Director for Community and Environmental
Services is authorised, after consultation with the Heads of Legal,
HR and Property Services to commence negotiations and agreement
with Lancashire County Council School Meals Service (LCCSMS), with
a view to Blackpool Catering Services being transferred under their
control and management, taking into account key areas and legal
processes as follows:
 
-       
Proceed with the novation of existing Service Level
Agreements (SLAs) to Lancashire County Council School Meals
Service, subject to agreement from the relevant schools and academy
trusts;
-       
Undertake formal consultation with recognised trade
unions and affected staff (114) in line with the Transfer of
Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006
(TUPE);
-       
Arrange for the transfer of the Highfield Central
Production Unit (CPU) under a lease agreement to Lancashire County
Council School Meals Service as part of the service transition,
including an appropriate agreement in relation to the equipment and
delivery vehicles;
-       
Agree a £100,000 contribution to the
redevelopment of Central Production Unit, in order that it can
provide to a wider audience across Blackpool and the Fylde
Coast;
-       
Transfer all consumables (stock and light equipment)
linked to the delivery of current Service Level Agreement, where
this is mutually agreed between parties; and
-       
To carry out a market testing procurement exercise
in relation to the operation of the Anchorsholme Park
café.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Communities and Wellbeing has decided to transfer Blackpool Catering Service to Lancashire County Council School Meals Service to address financial viability concerns and changing market dynamics.

content:
To
set out the proposed fees and charges for Planning for
2026-2027.
 

The
Leader of the Council agreed the recommendations as outlined above
namely:
 

To
maintain the national charging schedule for statutory planning
applications as detailed in Appendix ‘A’ with effect
from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.

 

To
increase the Council’s pre-application advice fees in-line
with inflation (currently stated to be 3.5% by the Bank of England)
as detailed in Appendix ‘B’ with effect from 1 April
2026 to 31 March 2027. 

 

To
maintain the Council’s charging schedule in terms of the
level of fees retained when invalid applications are not
subsequently made valid and to increase fees for miscellaneous
items by 3.5% as detailed in Appendix ‘C’ with effect
from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. 

 

To agree
that the fees charged can be reduced from these rates in
exceptional circumstances with the agreement of the Growth and
Prosperity Programme Director.

content:
The
Executive resolved as follows:
 
1.
        To
agree that Appendices 5a, 5b and 5c to the Executive report, are
not for publication by virtue of Paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Schedule
12A of the Local Government Act 1972 as these document included
detailed costings that enable the Blackpool Enterprise Zone to be
viable. The publication of such information could prejudice
continuing and future negotiations.
 
2.
        To
note:
 

a)              
The progress made on the delivery of the Enterprise
Zone Masterplan including supporting more than c2700 new jobs to
the end of December 2025, with an updated job census due to be
undertaken Quarter 2 2026.
 

b)              
The total estimated cumulative expenditure from
April 2016 to end of March 2027 of circa £64.85m, which
remains within the overall estimated whole life Enterprise Zone
budget envelope of £88m.
 

c)              
To note the funding approved on 17th March 2025 in
Executive Decision outlined planned expenditure of £54.17m to
year end 25/26. The current anticipated spend at the end of this
financial year will be circa £45.62m, with circa £8.55m
carry forward into next financial year to complete the Eastern
Gateway access road and associated works, Airport East highway and
utility provision. The further request for authority to spend up to
£64.85m (inclusive of the £8.55m carry forward) will
provide the relevant funding to commence initial implementation
plans and site assembly for the delivery of Silicon
Sands.
 

d)              
To note that only the carry over expenditure of
£8.55 million will be committed as a result of this
report.  Any expenditure beyond that of
more than 5% of the £54.17m will be brought back to the
Executive for approval along with clarity on how that will be
funded.
 

e)              
The forecast expenditure budget set out in Appendix
5a, to the Executive report, illustrates the position to the end of
March 2027 (£64.85m). The increased whole life cumulative
expenditure estimate remains at £88.15m at present values to
March 2041, resulting in an estimated whole life shortfall of
£2.92m at today’s prices.
 

f)               
That the anticipated cost of prudential borrowing
required to meet approved expenditure will exceed the net income
from retained rates growth and lands sales income over the next
five years and will require additional funding to be
identified.
 

g)              
The higher levels of financial risk associated with
the overall whole life expenditure and income forecasts, given the
length of the project and impact of external influences.
 

h)              
The potential for the Enterprise Zone to support
more than 5,000 job opportunities across the Fylde coast and
generate circa £2bn of cumulative Gross Value Added and
achieve a whole life operating surplus.
 
3.         To
approve:
 

a)              
The authorisation of the Director of Place and the
Section 151 Officer to explore all methods of mitigating the
forecast cash flow shortfall as shown in Appendix 5a, to the
Executive report, and seek any subsequent approvals that may be
necessary.
 

b)              
The carry forward of the remaining approved total
budget of circa £8.55m to the end March 2027, as noted in
resolution 2 c.
 

c)              
The approach in relation to the site assembly,
investment and development of infrastructure within the Blackpool
Airport Enterprise Zone, which is required to enable the
development of Silicon Sands as set out in Section 3.4.
 

d)              
The total estimated cumulative expenditure from
April 2016 to end of March 2027 of circa £64.85m to March
2028 inclusive of the estimated £8.85m carry over included
within the existing approval.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve funding and plans for the Blackpool Enterprise Zone, aiming to create jobs and develop infrastructure.

content:
The
report is provided in response to the Executive Paper
(EX39/2025
10th November 2025) and the decision to note the draft
list of potential Pride in Place Impact Fund schemes outlined in
the report, and for the approval of the final allocation of funding
to be delegated to the Director of Place, in consultation with the
Leader of the Council”. This is the first of what will be
several Officer Non-Key Decisions relating to projects to be
included in the Pride in Place Impact Fund programme, which will be
brought forward for approval as soon as they are ready to be
implemented.
 
This
report seeks formal approval for £265,000 capital grant
funding to be used to fund various projects that will support
businesses located in South Shore
 

That the sum of £265,000
from the Pride and Place Impact Fund is allocated to the following
projects:
 

a)    
South Shore

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Community Safety, Street Scene and Neighbourhoods
purpose:
The proposed Parking Services
fees and charges for 2026/27.
content:
The proposed Parking Services
fees and charges for 2026/27.
 

The Cabinet Member agreed the recommendations as outlined above
namely:
 

1.    
To agree the schedule of on and off-street parking
tariffs for each parking area as set out within the attached
schedule at Appendix A, subject to consultation, with effect from
April 1, 2026. Note that these tariffs will show a blanket increase
of 3.4% rounded to the nearest 10 pence and reflects the first
tariff increase since 2022 for the majority of sites. The increase
follows the impact of the rising operational and maintenance costs
and remains below the current UK RPI rate of 4.2% (Dec
2025).
 

2.    
To agree the schedule of the business and
residential permit rates as set out within the attached schedule at
Appendix A. Note the recommendation is for these permit charges to
remain unchanged for the financial year commencing April 1,
2026.
 

3.    
To agree a schedule of charges for parking bay
suspension and dispensations as set out within the attached
schedule at Appendix A. Note the recommendation is for these
charges to be aligned with neighbouring Councils and will reflect
the first charge increase since 2018.
 

4.    
To agree the introduction of two additional tariff
time bands for South Beach Car Park. This will provide additional
parking flexibility on parking periods at that site.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Community Safety, Street Scene and Neighbourhoods has decided to approve a 3.4% increase in parking tariffs for 2026/27, unchanged permit rates, alignment of charges with neighbouring Councils, and the introduction of two additional tariff time bands for South Beach Car Park.

content:
The Executive resolved as
follows:
 

To
recommend to the Council that the 2026/27 Housing Revenue Account
budget as set out in Appendix 3a, to the Executive report, is
approved.

 

To
recommend to the Council that rents for all Housing Revenue account
properties are increased by 4.8% in 2026/27 to maintain the health
and future viability of the Housing Revenue Account in line with
official guidance.

 

To
recommend to the Council that in line with government rent
flexibility provisions additional rent increases of 5% are applied
at re-let to general needs formula rent properties and 10% to
supported housing.

 

To
recommend to the Council that the minimum level of Housing Revenue
Account balances remain protected at £1 million, as
previously agreed.

 
 

To
recommend to the Council that Housing Revenue Account service
charges (as detailed in Appendix 3b, to the Executive report) and
other General Fund service charges (as detailed in Appendix 3c, to
the Executive report) are charged as outlined.

 

To
note that once the principles are approved by Government that a
rent convergence policy will be presented for approval.
topline: The Executive has decided to recommend to the Council the approval of the 2026/27 Housing Revenue Account budget and rent increases to maintain the viability of the account.

content:
The Executive resolved as
follows:
 
1.    
To recommend to Council to approve the Capital Programme for 2026/27 and
exemplifications for 2027/28 and 2028/29 as set out at Appendix 6a,
to the Executive report.
 

To
recommend to Council to agree that Executive approvals will
continue to be required for all prudential borrowing schemes
(reference paragraph 6.10).

 

To
recommend to Council to agree to continue with the Single Capital
Pot approach as outlined in Section 6 with an increased top slice
of 25% to allow for investment in key priority areas and overspends
that are not otherwise fundable (reference paragraph
6.11).

 

To
recommend to Council to approve the Capital Prudential Indicators
as identified in Appendix 6b, to the Executive report.
topline: The Executive has decided to recommend approval of the Capital Programme and exemplifications, continuation of prudential borrowing schemes, and an increase in the Single Capital Pot approach.

content:
The Executive resolved as
follows:
 

1.    
To recommend to Council the level of net expenditure
for the draft General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 of
£229,630,000 (ref. paragraph 6.11 and Appendix 4a, to the
Executive report)
 

2.    
To recommend to Council a level of budget savings of
£12.5m noting that this amount had been updated following the
Government’s Final Financial Settlement, approval of the
associated Flexible Use of Capital Receipts Strategy (Appendix 4g
to the Executive report) and incorporating a Council Tax increase
of 4.99% made up of 2.99% plus a 2% Adult Social Care
precept.
 

3.    
To note that the precepts for Fire and Police will
be reported to Full Council on 23 February 2026 as the rates are
not agreed until 23 February 2026 and week commencing the 16
February 2026 respectively.
 

4.    
To recommend to Council that the Chief Executive be
authorised to take any necessary steps to ensure any staffing
savings are achieved (ref. paragraph 6.16)
 

5.    
To recommend to Council the proposed use of the
Dedicated Schools Grant Budget for 2026/27 (ref. paragraph 6.9.1
and Appendix 4c, to the Executive report).
 

6.    
To recommend to Council the allocation of schools
funding for 2026/27 (ref. paragraph 6.9.1 and Appendix 4c, to the
Executive report).
 

7.    
To recommend to Council a target level of working
balances of £7.8m by 31 March 2027 (ref. paragraph
7.6.13).
 

8.    
To recommend to Council that due regard is given to
the robustness of the estimates and the adequacy of reserves in the
budget proposals for 2026/27 (ref. section 7.6).
 

9.    
To consider any further facts, information and
stakeholder feedback which may emerge and report the details to the
meeting of the Council on 23 February 2026.
topline: The Executive has recommended budget allocations and savings measures for the General Fund Revenue Budget 2026/27 to Council.

content:
The Executive resolved as
follows:
 

To
recommend to the Council to approve the Treasury Management
Strategy 2026/27 including both the Borrowing and Investment
Strategies which are set out in Appendix 7c and Appendix 7d, to the
Executive report.

 

To
recommend to the Council  to adopt the
Treasury Management Policy Statement, three key principles and four
clauses taken from the Treasury Management in the Public Services
Code of Practice and Cross-Sectoral Guidance Notes (2021 Edition)
and set out in Appendix 7b, to the Executive report.

 

To
recommend to the Council  to approve the
revised Prudential Indicators and Limits for 2025/26 and the new
Prudential Indicators and Limits for 2026/2027 - 2028/29 which are
set out in Appendix 7e, to the Executive report.

 

To
recommend to the Council to approve the Minimum Revenue
Provision

Policy Statement for 2026/27, which will ensure a prudent
Minimum Revenue Provision charge in the annual statement of
accounts. The policy is set out within Appendix 7f to the Executive
report.
topline: The Executive has decided to recommend the approval of the Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 and related policies to the Council.

content:
The Executive agreed the
recommendations as outlined above namely:
 

1.    
To note the report.  
 

2.    
To require the respective directors, Chief Executive
and Director of Resources to continue to closely monitor and manage
service financial and operational performances, specifically Growth
and Prosperity, Children’s Services, Place, Strategic Leisure
Assets, Adult Services and the wholly-owned companies.
 

3.    
To note the Scrutiny Leadership Board will continue
to independently review the financial and operational performances
of Council services.
 

4.    
To continue to lobby central government
(Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Department
for Health and Social Care and Department for Education in
particular) along with local authority peers and networks and the
Local Government Association for the funding necessary to cope with
the burdens and demands presenting as a result of inflationary
pressures and demographic demands upon statutory services.
 
5.    
To continue to work towards target working balances
of £7m by 1 April 2026.
topline: The Executive has decided to closely monitor service performances, lobby central government for funding, and work towards target working balances.

exception.

content:
The Executive agreed the
recommendation as outlined above namely:
 
1.    
To note the report.  
 
2.    
To require the respective directors, Chief Executive
and Director of Resources to continue to closely monitor and manage
service financial and operational performances, specifically Growth
and Prosperity, Children’s Services, Place, Strategic Leisure
Assets, Adult Services and the wholly-owned companies.
 
3.    
To note the Scrutiny Leadership Board will continue
to independently review the financial and operational performances
of Council services.
 
4.    
To continue to lobby central government (Ministry of
Housing, Communities and Local Government, Department for Health
and Social Care and Department for Education in particular) along
with local authority peers and networks and the Local Government
Association for the funding necessary to cope with the burdens and
demands presenting as a result of inflationary pressures and
demographic demands upon statutory services.
 
5.    
To continue to work towards target working balances
of £7m by 1 April 2026.
topline: The Executive has decided to closely monitor service performances, lobby for funding, and work towards target balances.

content:

Requirement figure for the 2024/25 accounts.

content:
The Executive resolved
as follows:                                                                                      
 

1.    
To agree that the
decision is exempt from call in due to the need to make a
submission to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government (MHCLG) by 28 November 2025.
 

2.    
To note the observations made at the special Council
meeting held on 18 November 2025 regarding the proposed submission
on local government reorganisation in Lancashire.
 

3.    
To approve the proposal attached as
Blackpool’s business case for local government reorganisation
in Lancashire.
 

4.    
To approve that as part of the proposal, a request
is made to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government for a modification order under Section 7 of The Local
Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007 to deliver
boundary changes alongside the base business case as set out in the
proposal document.
 

5.    
To authorise the Leader of the Council to submit the
Council’s proposal for local government reorganisation in
Lancashire to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government.

 

6.    
To delegate authority to the Chief Executive,
following consultation with the Leader of the Council, to approve
any minor amendments to the proposal that may be required, to
ensure submission before the deadline.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve Blackpool's business case for local government reorganisation in Lancashire.

content:
The Executive agreed the
recommendations as outlined above namely:
 

To
agree to the change to the current High Pressure Sodium (SON) and
Cosmopolis (CPO)  street lighting to
Light Emitting Diode (LED) luminaires.

 

To
agree to seek advice from National Infrastructure and Service
Transformation Authority  (NISTA) who
advise on PFI Contracts, and have offered Blackpool Council,
together with its specialist legal advisors, Local Partnerships,
the benefit of their experience free of charge to assist in the
Deed of Variation changes.

 

To
fund this scheme at a cost of £6.85m by Prudential Borrowing
of £3.75m, the borrowing to be repaid from energy savings
resulting from the installation of Light Emitting Diodes. The
residual sum of £3.1m to be contributed by Community Lighting
Partnership from maintenance monies. These costs also include
implementation of lighting to Stanley Park.

 

To
note that following the successful completion of the Light Emitting
Diodes replacement savings of £930,000 per year (based on
current energy costs ) will be used  to
repay the associated Prudential Borrowing.

 

To
ensure there is appropriate funding available to manage the project
financially, that the energy budget of £2.1m is ring fenced
for this scheme.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve the change from High Pressure Sodium and Cosmopolis street lighting to Light Emitting Diode luminaires.

content:

1.

2.    
To require the respective directors, Chief Executive
and Director of Resources to continue to closely monitor and manage
service financial and operational performances, specifically Growth
and Prosperity, Children’s Services, Parking Services,
Strategic Leisure Assets, Place, Adult Services and the
wholly-owned companies.
 
3.    
To note the Scrutiny Leadership Board will continue
to independently review the financial and operational performances
of Council services.
 
4.    
To continue to lobby central government (Ministry of
Housing, Communities and Local Government, Department for Health
and Social Care and Department for Education in particular) along
with local authority peers and networks and the Local Government
Association for the funding necessary to cope with the burdens and
demands presenting as a result of inflationary pressures and
demographic demands upon statutory services.
 
5.    
To continue to work towards target working balances
of £8m by 1 April 2026.

content:
The Executive resolved as
follows:
 
1. To agree that
Appendix 6b to the Executive report, is not for publication by
virtue of Paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Schedule 12A of the Local
Government Act 1972 as it includes detailed costings that enable
the Silicon Sands scheme to be viable. The publication of such
information could prejudice continuing and future
negotiations.
 
2. To note the contents of the
report.
 
3. 
To delegate to the Chief Executive, after consultation with the
Leader of the Council, authority to agree a preferred bidder for
the Technology Exemplar at the Blackpool Airport Enterprise
Zone. 
 
4. 
To authorise the Head of Legal Services to enter into all required
legal documentation in connection with the development of the
Technology Exemplar
 
5. 
To authorise, subject to suitable procurement, the securing of
appropriate contractual relationships with consultants as required
to progress, promote and deliver Silicon Sands.
 
6. To confirm an initial budget
allocation of £450,000 within the overall approved Enterprise
Zone budget envelope for progression of Silicon Sands.
 
7. To approve submission of an
outline planning application to Fylde Borough Council  seeking  consent for
the development of a 6MW capacity Data Centre , and associated
plant, together with 20,000 sq.ft of office/research and
development  accommodation and provision
for connections to a proposed District Heating system.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for the development of the Silicon Sands scheme at Blackpool Airport Enterprise Zone.

content:
The Executive agreed the
recommendation as outlined above namely:
 
1.    
To note the report.  
 
2.    
To require the respective directors, Chief Executive
and Director of Resources to continue to closely monitor and manage
service financial and operational performances, specifically Growth
and Prosperity, Children’s Services, Parking Services,
Strategic Leisure Assets, Place, Adult Services and the
wholly-owned companies.
 
3.    
To note the Scrutiny Leadership Board will continue
to independently review the financial and operational performances
of Council services.
 
4.    
To continue to lobby central government (Ministry of
Housing, Communities and Local Government, Department for Health
and Social Care and Department for Education in particular) along
with local authority peers and networks and the Local Government
Association for the funding necessary to cope with the burdens and
demands presenting as a result of inflationary pressures and
demographic demands upon statutory services.
 

5.    
To continue to work towards target working balances
of £8m by 1 April 2026.
topline: The Executive has decided to approve recommendations for closely monitoring service performances and lobbying central government for necessary funding.

content:
The Executive agreed
the recommendations as outlined above namely:
 

1.    
To note the progress on the delivery of Central
Housing Regeneration programme.
 

2.    
To suspend the usual re-letting of these units to
enable full vacancy to be achieved.
 

3.    
To resolve to commence activity to identify
alternative provision for the use of the building at the corner of
Central Drive and Rigby Road and to seek a formal decision once a
relocation plan has been outlined.
 

4.    
To note that CPO Guidance Home Loss Payments
(Prescribed Amounts) (England) Regulations 2023 will be followed in
supporting those residents being required to relocate, providing
Homes Loss and Disturbance payments, where applicable.
 

5.    
To allow that once full vacancy has been achieved,
and subject to the relevant planning approvals, to demolish the
existing two blocks totalling 12 flats to enable Central Housing
Regeneration Phase 1 redevelopment.
